cohort: The study included 1312 women enrolled during their first trimester of pregnancy at ARNAS Garibaldi Nesima in Catania, Italy, between December 2020 and October 2023.
finding: Maternal education, smoking status, mode of delivery, and gestational weight gain significantly influence breastfeeding practices and adherence to WHO recommendations, with higher education, non-smoking, and spontaneous delivery associated with better outcomes.
mod_finding: Women who had a spontaneous delivery were more likely to breastfeed (OR = 1.461; 95% CI: 1.090-1.958; p = 0.011) compared to those with other modes of birth.
